svg.text: Kart Electrical Wiring — Power & Shutdown Circuit
Signal & Control Wiring — Pedals, Mode Switch, Steering
Steering PID in ESP32: reads AS5600 angle → computes error → drives Cytron PWM/DIR
1. Battery (48 V) feeds the terminal block. Motor controller draws BAT+ and GND; outputs 3 phases (U, V, W) to the motor via the same terminal block.
2. Buck regulator steps 48 V down to 12 V, distributed through WAGO connectors.
3. The 12 V rail feeds the Shutdown Circuit (SDC): a series chain of kill switches, impact switch, and RES (with manual bypass).
4. SDC current flows through the relay coil (pin 86 → 85), then to ground via kart_medulla’s N-channel MOSFET.
5. When the relay is energized, its N.O. contacts (30 → 87) close, completing the motor controller’s KEY circuit and enabling drive.
6. Any open switch in the SDC chain de-energizes the relay → contacts open → motor controller disabled.
7. Pedal sensors (linear Hall, 0–5 V) always feed analog signals to kart_medulla for data logging and/or autonomous control.
8. SPDT mode switch on the dashboard selects throttle source: manual (pedal → motor ctrl directly) or autonomous (ESP32 DAC → motor ctrl).
9. Steering: ESP32 PID reads AS5600 angle sensor (I2C) and drives Cytron MD25HV H-bridge (PWM + DIR) to control the steering motor.
10. Brake pedal signal is read by kart_medulla; its DAC output (CMD_BRK) feeds the motor controller’s brake input.
